The country known for the Eiffel Tower is France.

Based on your nostalgic mood and appreciation for the psychological depth of Hitchcock and Kubrick, I recommend the 1941 classic **The Maltese Falcon**. Directed by John Huston, this film is a cornerstone of the film noir genre and fits perfectly within the Golden Age of Hollywood mystery category. It features a complex, enigmatic plot and sharp, witty dialogue that will appeal to fans of intricate storytelling. If you prefer something with a slightly more psychological edge reminiscent of Hitchcock’s suspense, **Double Indemnity** (1944) is another excellent choice, offering a tense cat-and-mouse game between an insurance salesman and a femme fatale.
